text:
Maya (People Ops): quick Q — new hire Tom started 12/28/25 during the payroll vendor cutover and was auto-enrolled at 4% pre-tax. He just asked to do the age‑50+ catch-up for 2025. Vendor said cutover closed 12/31 and they 'don't accept retro elections', but Tom wants to max the 2025 catch-up. can payroll/do benefits do an off-cycle to allocate additional deferral to 2025? cc @Ravi

Ravi (Payroll): short answer: maybe. We can run an off-cycle adjustment but need the vendor to accept a retro contribution posting for plan year 2025. If PlanCo will accept an employer remittance labeled for 2025, we can push an off-cycle deduction. Important: whether it's pre-tax or Roth catch-up matters for tax reporting. Also if we already filed 2025 W-2s, adding deferral will require a W-2c.

Ines (Benefits Ops): Plan doc check: the plan allows catch-up contributions for eligible participants and can accept late remittances if submitted with the correct allocation forms and signed employee consent. PlanCo's practical rule: they will post retro amounts if we send their "Late Contribution Allocation" form + ACH/check and include plan year coding. I'll ping our PlanCo rep.

Tom (IC, Eng): I want pre-tax catch-up. My math: I hit $3,500 pretax in 2025 and would like to add $4,000 to reach the $7,500 limit. I'm comfortable with whatever forms needed.

Maya (People Ops): great — next steps: (1) @Ravi confirm payroll can produce a one-off 401(k) pre-tax catch-up for $4,000 and mark it for plan year 2025, (2) @Ines confirm PlanCo will accept and what form + remittance they need, (3) we confirm W-2 impact (W-2 vs W-2c).

Ravi (Payroll): I'll talk to the vendor tomorrow. If they accept a contribution file, they want these columns in CSV: emp_id,last_name,first_name,contribution_type,catchup_amount,plan_year,payroll_date,remittance_method

Ravi (Payroll): sample row we can send:```12345,Doe,Tom,401k_catchup,4000,2025,2026-03-15,ACH``` vendor asked specifically for 'plan_year' field = 2025 so they credit the prior year.

Ines (Benefits Ops): PlanCo replied: they will accept the late allocation for 2025 if we send their Late Contribution Allocation form + the CSV + ACH remittance. They require the employee signature for catch-up consent (we have e-sign on file). They also noted: if we already transmitted 2025 Form W-2 to SSA, PlanCo will accept the allocation but payroll must issue a W-2c to correct employee deferrals.

erica.bot: payroll-offcycle-bot created ticket #PR-5723 and scheduled tentative off-cycle for 2026-03-15 pending approvals.

Ravi (Payroll): confirmed — we can run the off-cycle 3/15. I will: run off-cycle to collect $4,000, tag as 2025_catchup, send CSV & ACH to PlanCo, and if applicable prepare W-2c instructions to People Ops for signature routing.

Maya (People Ops): thanks all. I'll confirm Tom's e-sign for the catch-up and attach it to the PlanCo form. Tom — can you confirm you're OK with payroll issuing a W-2c if needed?

Tom (IC, Eng): yep fine, thanks for the help.

Maya (People Ops): closing loop — I'll upload the signed consent to the vendor form and ping when PlanCo confirms receipt. :thumbsup:
